content:
Maya Chen: Heads up — saw a ~12% spike in invoice-preview estimates for EU this morning during the canary rollback window. Seems correlated with route-tag stripping + sampling config. Posting logs + query snippets. cc @Samir @Priya
Samir Patel: ugh, can you paste the exact time window and sample tenant ids?
Maya Chen: window: 2026-03-19T08:12:00Z -> 08:22:00Z. tenant ids: t-5832, t-1f9b. quick grep: `router.log | grep "route_tag=null" | grep 2026-03-19T08:1` shows a bunch of `route_tag=null` from edge-proxy v2.3.1
Priya Rao: that proxy version had the tag-strip patch for GDPR headers, might be related. sample query I ran against ingest: `SELECT count(*) FROM metering.events WHERE route_tag IS NULL AND region='eu' AND ts BETWEEN ...` -> 184k events in that 10m. baseline is ~8k.
Jordan Lee: console impact? invoice preview for those tenants showed +11% compared to last snapshot. Customers might see surprising preview numbers in Console -> Billing -> Invoice preview.
Maya Chen: exact preview snapshot ids: preview_20260319_0815 vs preview_20260318_0815. Diff shows token delta concentrated on streaming sessions with `route='fallback'`
Alex Gomez: can we confirm whether sampling was applied before or after tag stripping? If sampling sees no tag it might fallback to higher-sample path.
Priya Rao: checked the canary rollout policy: we patched the tag middleware in proxy, but sampling decisions happen in the edge-router after header normalization. The order is: header-normalize -> sampling -> route-resolve. If the normalization removed tag header, sampling got a null and hit default sample weight -> heavier inclusion.
Samir Patel: that explains the jump. Default sample weight is 1.0 for null tags; normal weights are ~0.05 for many routes. How did this not trigger our canary telemetry?
billing-bot: alert: invoice_preview_delta_eu > 10% for 2 tenants (t-5832, t-1f9b) at 2026-03-19T08:18:12Z. Incident ID: INV-20260319-0818
Alex Gomez: we need a short-term mitigation: either revert tag-strip patch on the canary or temporarily set default sampling weight for null tags to 0.05. Which is faster?
Priya Rao: revert on canary is a 1-command deploy but rollback has other deps. Changing default sampling weight is a config flip in router service — I can push a hotfix in 10 minutes.
Maya Chen: hotfix seems safer for now. Priya, if you flip default sampling weight, can you also add a metric: `sampling.null_tag_ratio` by region?
Priya Rao: yes, will do. Also adding alert if null_tag_ratio > 0.02 for >5m.
Samir Patel: follow-up: we should adjust invoice-preview logic to ignore sampled events where route_tag is null and sample_weight != configured_default. Or annotate preview with a small tooltip explaining canary sampling noise.
Jordan Lee: UX note: show 'preview affected by canary sampling' banner when preview snapshot uses data during a rollout window. Minimal text and link to docs.
Alex Gomez: ops checklist: 1) Priya push hotfix (set default weight 0.05) 2) Maya re-run preview snapshots for affected tenants 3) Samir open a short postmortem doc and link to rollout gating checklist 4) Jordan add console banner PR 5) add ingestion metric and alert.
Priya Rao: hotfix pushed at 2026-03-19T08:28:03Z, verified sampling weight back to 0.05 in router-metrics. `router.metrics.sampling_weight_default{region='eu'} = 0.05`
Maya Chen: re-ran previews for t-5832/t-1f9b, diffs drop to +0.8% and +1.2% respectively. I'll update the ticket and ping support.
Samir Patel: created postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/tickets/INV-20260319-0818 (added timeline, root cause, mitigation, and follow-ups)
Jordan Lee: filing a small console PR for the banner, will target tomorrow morning.
Alex Gomez: thanks team. Longer term follow-ups: - move sampling decision upstream (before header normalization) OR ensure normalization preserves route tags for sampling - add unit test for canary tag-strip interaction - add preview-sensitivity flag to invoice previews to de-emphasize canary windows
Maya Chen: agreed. closing thread after postmortem updates. :thumbsup:
